characteristics.cultivar: Distinct Dan Cong lineage with 'Ba Xian' aroma profile

description.short: Aromatic Dan Cong with an unusual name and a vibrant honey-floral flavor despite its 'startling' title
description.overview: One of the most talked-about Dan Cong teas due to its curious name, which in no way reflects its true taste — the tea itself is fragrant, sweet, and floral.
description.aroma: Floral and honeyed, with fruity notes
description.taste: Sweet, floral, with a full body and the mineral undertone of Phoenix Mountain
description.processing: Classic Dan Cong craftsmanship: sun withering → vigorous shaking → kill-green → rolling into strips → baking/roasting

history.origin: According to one popular story, a local farmer, wanting to prevent competitors from copying his prized cultivar, deliberately gave the tea an unappealing name to disguise its true worth.
history.development: Despite the comical origin of its name, the tea gained tremendous popularity precisely through the striking contrast between its name and its exquisite, refined flavor.
history.modern: Today it is sometimes marketed under more melodious alternative names (such as 'Golden Phoenix'), yet the original name remains by far the most famous and recognizable.
interestingFacts: It is one of the few teas in the world whose global fame is partially driven by its unconventional and memorable name.
Growers note that the bushes grow in distinctive yellowish soil (huang ni tu), which is believed to contribute to the tea's unique flavor profile.
